newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna finance boss new Austria finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Vienna finance boss new Austria finance minister.

text.p: Austria's chancellor-designate Viktor Klima on Friday named Vienna City finance chief Rudolf Edlinger as the country's new finance minister, sources in the ruling Social Democratic party said.
The treasury post became vacant over the weekend when Franz Vranitzky named Klima his successor as chancellor and Social Democratic Party leader.

The Social Democrat source, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed an Austrian state radio report that Edlinger would step into the breach and seek to guide Austria into a single European currency. "It's him," the source said.
There was no immediate confirmation from the finance ministry.

Austrian radio said Klima had presented his Social Democrat ministerial line-up to President Thomas Klestil. No changes are expected among ministers of the conservative People's Party, which govern in coalition with the dominant Social Democrats.

Social Democrat Edlinger, 56, has served as the City of Vienna's finance councillor since November 1994 and has borne responsibility for by far Austria's biggest regional budget, with annual expenditure of around 134 billion schillings ($11.68 billion).
"Vienna is losing an outstanding finance chief and Austria is gaining an excellent finance minister," Austrian radio quoted Vienna mayor Michael Haeupl as saying.

Edlinger, a professional lithographer, was a key player in a political team that two weeks ago hammered out a coalition deal over the sale of Austria's most famous bank Creditanstalt to market leader Bank Austria.
The heavy-set smoker had insisted earlier this week that he was not a candidate to take over the finance portfolio and had set his sights on retirement by the year 2000. ($1=11.47 schillings)
